subject.title: Feature Request: Surface API provider name in error/overload messages

question: Should OpenClaw expose only provider/model, or also profile presence and trigger, in shared channel-visible transient provider error replies?
rationale: The core formatter can implement the provider-name request, but the exact diagnostic fields shown in Telegram and other shared transports are a product and privacy boundary rather than a purely mechanical fix.

options.title: Provider/Model In Chat, Extras In Metadata
options.body: Show the failed provider/model in user-facing transient error copy and keep profile presence or trigger in logs/lifecycle metadata unless maintainers explicitly approve wider shared-chat diagnostics.

options.title: Accept Broader Diagnostic Copy
options.body: Allow the linked PR direction to show provider/model/profile=active/trigger in chat after refresh, authMode preservation, and Telegram-visible proof.

options.title: Pause Core Copy Changes
options.body: Leave the issue open but do not land a core formatter change until maintainers decide provider diagnostics should be handled elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Provider/Model In Chat, Extras In Metadata
recommendation.body: Show the failed provider/model in user-facing transient error copy and keep profile presence or trigger in logs/lifecycle metadata unless maintainers explicitly approve wider shared-chat diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the current authMode formatter contract that any transient provider-context fix must preserve and are the clearest owner from current history for the provider/auth boundary.
